title: Architectural Material Lab with Duck Mascot Guide
description: The user enters a virtual architectural material testing laboratory where ShaderBall2 models serve as material sample pedestals arranged in a semicircular showroom. A Duck mascot acts as an interactive guide that waddles to each pedestal when clicked, triggering material property panels. Users configure architectural surface materials by adjusting roughness, metalness, color, and environment map intensity across multiple shader balls, then validate their selections against target specifications.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements an architectural material testing lab. Load both ShaderBall2.glb and Duck.glb using GLTFLoader from CDN. Clone ShaderBall2 five times and arrange them in a semicircular arc (radius 6 units) on a reflective ground plane resembling polished concrete. Each shader ball sits on a rectangular pedestal (BoxGeometry) labeled Material 1 through 5 using CSS2DRenderer overlays. Place the Duck model at the center of the arc, scaled to roughly half the shader ball height. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 4, 10) looking at the arc center. Add an HDR-style lighting rig with one DirectionalLight casting shadows, two RectAreaLights simulating studio softboxes, and ambient light at low intensity. Enable OrbitControls with constrained vertical rotation (10-70 degrees) and limited zoom range. Implement these interactions requiring parameter validation: (1) Click any shader ball to select it, highlighting its pedestal with an emissive outline. (2) The Duck animates (simple bobbing tween using Math.sin) and rotates to face the selected ball. (3) A floating HTML panel appears showing sliders for roughness (0-1, step 0.01), metalness (0-1, step 0.01), color picker, and envMapIntensity (0-3, step 0.1). (4) Adjusting sliders updates the selected shader ball material in real time using MeshStandardMaterial properties. (5) A target specification panel shows required values for each ball (e.g., Ball 1: roughness 0.3, metalness 0.9, color #C0C0C0). (6) A validate button checks all five balls against targets with a tolerance of 0.05, showing green checkmarks or red crosses per ball. (7) When all five pass validation, the Duck performs a celebratory spin animation and confetti particles emit from above. (8) A reset button restores all materials to defaults. Use requestAnimationFrame loop, proper disposal patterns, and responsive canvas sizing.
